title: Streaming contracts and graceful tool handoff: PRD clarifications, scope changes, and acceptance criteria
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Purpose: Codify the acceptance criteria for streaming structured output combined with tool/function invocation, with explicit handling for partial JSON frames, schema migrations, and failure modes. This ticket clarifies ambiguous PRD items and captures scope adjustments from the engineering review.

Background: Several teams have implemented streaming JSON and tool calling independently; discrepancies exist around schema enforcement, client-visible error semantics, and whether the runtime should attempt automatic retries or fallback text. This PRD clarifies those behaviors for the next release and establishes contract tests and telemetry expectations.
scope_changes: Original PRD included automatic synchronous retries on tool invocation failures; reduced scope to defining retry recommendation and a server-side retry counter exposed in telemetry instead of automated retries.
Dropped: runtime-level schema transformations (e.g., coercing types). We will instead fail-fast with clear error codes and a migration guide for consumers.
Added: explicit contract test harness for truncated streaming JSON and for mixed-mode outputs (partial JSON + plain text suffix).
acceptance_criteria: Schema validation: Streaming producer must emit a top-level 'envelope' object per documented schema version header (field: schema_version). Consumer tests must pass for versions v1 and v1.1. Any deviation leads to a 422 runtime event with error_code: 'schema_mismatch'.

Partial JSON frames: The runtime will support incremental JSON frames (ndjson-like fragments). Acceptance requires a canonical reassembly test where 1000 varied-length messages are streamed and reassembled into a single valid JSON object by client-side parser without data loss.

Tool invocation handshake: When the model signals a tool call, the streaming output must include a single well-formed 'tool_call' object with fields: tool_name, arguments (object), call_id (uuid). Acceptance requires test validating unique call_id per invocation and proper attribution in audit logs.

Tool failure modes: If an external tool returns a terminal error, the runtime MUST emit a terminal stream event with error_code from the allowed set: ['tool_unavailable','tool_timeout','tool_auth']. Acceptance requires that the client receives the final event and the system logs a correlated trace_id to the console dashboard.

Fallback behavior: If schema validation fails mid-stream, the service must not silently switch to plain text. Instead it should emit an error frame per the streaming protocol and close the stream. Acceptance requires QA to trigger a schema violation and confirm the stream closure and an administratively-visible alert in the rollout dashboard.

Streaming recovery: For consumer-initiated reconnect within 15s using the same call_id, the runtime must accept a resume request and replay missing frames when available. Acceptance requires a simulated 10s disconnect and successful resume with deduplication checks.

Backpressure and rate limits: The runtime must send 'backpressure' advisory frames when queue depth exceeds configured SLO thresholds. Acceptance requires stress tests at 4x normal throughput demonstrating backpressure frames are emitted and downstream clients honor them in at least 90% of cases in the harness.

Telemetry & observability: For every streamed tool call, runtime must emit telemetry events: tool.call.start, tool.call.end, tool.call.error with metadata fields: call_id, model, schema_version, user_id (if available). Acceptance requires ingestion into the console pipeline and sample dashboard panels reflecting counts and p50/p95 latency within 24 hours.

Security: Arguments passed to tools must be redacted in logs per PII guidelines. Acceptance requires a synthetic test where sensitive tokens are present in arguments and audit logs show redaction markers, not raw tokens.

Backward compatibility: If client specifies accept_schema: 'v1' in request metadata, runtime must downgrade structures where possible or return a clear incompatibility error. Acceptance requires interop tests between v1.1 producer and v1 consumer demonstrating graceful failure when downgrade is impossible.
test_cases: TC-01: Streamed valid envelope v1.1 - assert reassembled JSON equals golden fixture; assert no error frames emitted.
TC-02: Mid-stream schema mutation - intentionally change field type; assert runtime emits schema_mismatch error frame and closes stream; assert dashboard alert created.
TC-03: Tool invocation success - stream contains tool_call object; external mock tool returns success; assert tool.call.end telemetry and proper payload delivered to client.
TC-04: Tool invocation failure modes - mock tool returns 503 and auth failure; assert correct error_code frames and unique tracing.
TC-05: Truncated stream recovery - disconnect at byte boundary; reconnect with call_id; assert no duplicated objects post-reassembly.
TC-06: Backpressure - synthetic load 4x; verify backpressure frames emitted and client respects 2s throttling window.
TC-07: Log redaction - arguments contain 'password' key; verify logs contain '<REDACTED>' and not raw value.
TC-08: Version negotiation - client requests accept_schema:v1; producer emits v1.1 fields that cannot be downgraded; assert graceful incompatibility error.
open_questions: Q1: Should the runtime provide a pluggable transform hook for customers to register best-effort schema coercions? Engineering recommends not in this cycle; product to decide.
Q2: What is the allowed time window for resume and replay beyond 15s for Dedicated customers with higher SLAs? Proposed: configurable per-customer up to 5 minutes.
Q3: How should binary tool outputs (e.g., images) be streamed within the JSON envelope? Proposal: base64 with explicit content_type field; seek security review.
Q4: Do we want to expose an opt-in 'best-effort-auto-retry' flag to customers for tool invocations? Trade-off: hides failures from customers but can mask flaky integrations.
decisions: D1: No automated runtime-level retries for external tool failures this cycle; surface retry recommendations and telemetry instead.
D2: Fail-fast on schema violations; do not attempt silent coercion or implicit fallback to unstructured text.
D3: Resume semantics will be supported with a 15s default window and made configurable for Enterprise via Dedicated contracts.
D4: Tool argument redaction is mandatory for logs; visibility to customers via redaction metadata only.
